html:
Éamon de Valera was the leading figure of independent Ireland for half a century, as head of government for most years from 1932 to 1959 and then president until 1973.

Born in New York, he was a commander in the Easter Rising and escaped execution. He led Sinn Féin, opposed the Treaty and was on the losing side in the Civil War. In 1926 he founded Fianna Fáil, which won power in 1932.

He then dismantled the Treaty step by step. His constitution of 1937, approved by referendum, renamed the state Éire, or Ireland, and gave a special place to the Catholic Church. He kept Ireland neutral in the Second World War. His ideal of a rural, Catholic, Gaelic Ireland shaped the country until the economic opening of the 1960s.
sum: Éamon de Valera was the leading figure of independent Ireland for half a century, as head of government for most years from 1932 to 1959 and then president until 1973.
